tool_description: Persist one complete owner-scoped GHOST Skill as a new Skill or an immutable replacement in the explicitly selected CLI or GENERAL domain.
CLI and GENERAL use the same creation mechanism but separate artifacts and Skill Memory.
CLI Skills support the CLI learning policy; General Skills are created only when the user explicitly asks to save a General Skill in the current implementation.
server_instruction: Set skill_domain to exactly CLI or GENERAL. Never infer a cross-domain fallback and never use an ID returned from the other domain.

This tool creates exactly one Skill per call. If the CLI parent policy selected multiple independent Skill actions, call this tool sequentially once for each action and never more than three times for the complete user task.
The decision must be exactly CREATE_NEW_SKILL or UPDATE_EXISTING_SKILL. For NO_CHANGE, do not call this tool.

For CLI, factual Layer-1 execution feedback from the completed CLI task may justify automatic learning. Instructions explicitly provided by the user in the original task may also control what is saved and how it is grouped.
For GENERAL, create or update a Skill only when the user explicitly asks to save a General Skill. Ordinary prompt execution or General Skill retrieval alone must not create one.
Automatic learning from new user feedback provided only after the completed task remains outside the current implementation scope.

The user's explicit saving structure has priority. If the user requests every detail in one named Skill, create or update one complete Skill and do not split it. If the user requests separation, preserve the requested boundaries within the CLI parent limit of three Skill actions.

A neutral Skill should contain reusable operational methods. A deliberately task-specific Skill may contain exact targets, paths, named content, or a user-defined workflow when the user explicitly requests that information to be saved.
Without an explicit Skill-saving instruction, do not save one-off paths, named files, media choices, or other task-specific details merely because they appeared during execution.

Choose UPDATE_EXISTING_SKILL only when a relevant active Skill in the selected domain is wrong, incomplete, ambiguous, or missing a justified concrete rule. Pass every exact affected Skill ID returned by ghost_skill_loader for that same domain.

Use only tags currently present in the authenticated owner Skill tag catalog. Call ghost_skill_tag_settings with action show when the current catalog is not already known. Omit skill_tags or pass an empty list to assign the existing default automatically; never invent a tag.
Choose CREATE_NEW_SKILL only when no appropriate loaded Skill in the selected domain represents the intended reusable or explicitly requested capability. Pass an empty affected_skill_ids list.
An update is immutable. Provide one complete replacement Skill, preserving all proven correct instructions and changing only what the evidence or explicit user instruction justifies.
Do not add generic best practices, speculative improvements, unrelated architecture, invented failures, or invented environment facts.
Provide a clear human-readable title and one compact semantic description explaining what the Skill does and when it is relevant.
Only skill_description is embedded for candidate retrieval. The complete procedure belongs in skill_text and is loaded only after candidate selection.
The complete skill_text must remain within the 10000-token hard limit. This is a maximum, not a target.
GHOST owns the internal Skill ID, timestamped folder path, SKILL.md path, Memory record ID, Recall Key, and lifecycle status. Never invent those values.
If GHOST returns SKILL_NAME_ALREADY_EXISTS, load the returned existing_skill_id from the same domain and decide between NO_CHANGE and a justified UPDATE_EXISTING_SKILL.
If GHOST returns SKILL_UPDATE_BUSY, do not wait, retry repeatedly, or create a duplicate.
If GHOST reports a corrupted Skill registry or failed rollback, stop Skill creation and report the integrity failure.

field_descriptions.skill_domain: Exact isolated Skill domain: CLI for directly executable CLI guidance, or GENERAL for reusable context attached to a larger prompt.
field_descriptions.decision: Exactly CREATE_NEW_SKILL or UPDATE_EXISTING_SKILL. For NO_CHANGE, do not call this tool.
field_descriptions.skill_name: Stable semantic Skill name containing only letters, numbers, period, underscore, or hyphen. Name matching is owner-scoped and unique only inside the selected domain.
field_descriptions.skill_title: Clear human-readable title of the capability. This is returned with retrieval candidates and written into SKILL.md.
field_descriptions.skill_description: One compact, informative semantic paragraph describing what the Skill does and when it should be loaded. This value alone is embedded for retrieval.
field_descriptions.skill_text: Complete final Markdown instruction body for SKILL.md without the YAML header or repeated title. Preserve correct existing rules during an update. Maximum 10000 tokens.
field_descriptions.yaml_metadata: Optional additional YAML-compatible metadata. GHOST supplies name and description when absent.
field_descriptions.ragmem_title: Semantic Episode Title for the selected domain's Skill Memory representation.
field_descriptions.ragmem_description: Semantic Episode Description for the selected domain's Skill Memory episode.
field_descriptions.affected_skill_ids: For UPDATE_EXISTING_SKILL, exact active Skill IDs returned and loaded from the selected domain. For CREATE_NEW_SKILL, an empty list.
field_descriptions.notes: Optional factual lifecycle or implementation notes. Do not add speculative notes.
field_descriptions.skill_tags: Optional controlled Skill categories. Values must exist in the authenticated owner Skill tag catalog. Missing or empty uses the existing default tag.
